submission.natural_language_explanation: Previous-token copy head that fires when the current token continues a tight multi-token unit with the token before it: (a) word-internal pieces with no leading space and UTF-8 byte pieces of CJK/Arabic/Persian text (Kal|ining, acet|amin|ophen, Jet|Bra|ins, allclasses_|navbar; 1.6-4.7), and (b) fixed collocations, strongest for ' as' after ' such' (3.7-4.0), ' Names' after 'Committee on Antarctic' (5.0) and ' Historic' in 'National Register of Historic Places' (3.8). It is broad on prose: ordinary English sentences often cross the 1.23 line weakly (1.2-2.5), especially the first few tokens after an opener such as He/We/I/In/Later/Copyright, while texts opening with 'The' and made of whole-word tokens stay mostly quiet; predicted inactive (peak below 0.25) are comma-separated lists of integers where each number is one token (23/23 measured at 0.00, 7-17 tokens), and 'The <plural noun> were/are <one-token numbers with commas and 'and'>.' sentences (16/16, max 0.18).
